# Jesús Bolívar

> Venezuelan entrepreneur in education and fintech. Founder of UnoPago, the financial operating system for schools in Venezuela, and co-founder and CEO of Open Minds Early School in Oakland, California. Writes on Venezuela's macroeconomy and exchange-rate policy, and runs trail races.

Also known as: Chubeto, Jesus Bolivar, Jesús “Chubeto” Bolívar, Chubeto Bolívar.
Roles: Founder, UnoPago; Co-founder and CEO, Open Minds Early School.
Education: Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Harvard Kennedy School; Instituto Educacional Juan XXIII.
Based in: Oakland, California.

## Pages

- [Jesús Bolívar (Chubeto) · UnoPago, Open Minds Early School](https://www.bolivarjesus.com/): Jesús “Chubeto” Bolívar builds and invests in education: founder of UnoPago, payments for schools in Venezuela, and co-founder of Open Minds Early School.
- [Writing · Jesús Bolívar](https://www.bolivarjesus.com/blog/): Essays and data pieces by Jesús Bolívar on Venezuela's macroeconomy, on education, and on the plumbing that connects the two. Every chart names its source.
- [Running · Jesús Bolívar](https://www.bolivarjesus.com/running/): Jesús “Chubeto” Bolívar's running since 2011: trail races, half marathons, the SF Marathon and the Bryce Canyon 50K, with his trail routes and personal bests.
- [The Kangaroo Peg, 2026](https://www.bolivarjesus.com/KangarooPegRevisited2026/): Venezuela's exchange-rate regime from 2003 to 2026 and the path out of it: where the bolívar stands, where the economy must be by 2031, and the policy sequence that gets it there without asking the state to do the investing. An update of Bettocchi & Bolívar (2013).
- [La paridad canguro (Kangaroo Peg), 2026](https://www.bolivarjesus.com/KangarooPegRevisited2026/es/): El régimen cambiario venezolano de 2003 a 2026 y la salida: dónde está el bolívar, dónde tiene que estar la economía en 2031 y la secuencia de políticas que la lleva allí sin pedirle al Estado que sea el inversionista. Actualización de Bettocchi & Bolívar (2013).

## Running

- Jesús “Chubeto” Bolívar has run since 2011: 950 runs, 5,641 km and 54,021 m of climbing in 32 places, from Boston to Bryce Canyon, and 16 races.
- Best half marathon: 1:44:37 at the Berkeley Half Marathon, November 2023.
- Best marathon: 4:12:29 at the SF Marathon, July 2023.
- Best 30K: 3:24:21 at the Chabot 30K, February 2024.
- Longest run: 53.9 km at the Bryce Canyon Ultras, May 2023.
- Best placing: 2nd overall at the Mt. Umunhum Trail Conquest – Winter (half marathon), February 2024.
- Races: Oakland Hills Trail Run (Half marathon, October 2022, 2:31:18); SF Spartan Race (Half marathon, November 2022, 2:25:45); Fort Ord Trail Run (25K, January 2023, 2:58:04); Race to the Top of Mt Umunhum Vert Challenge (Half marathon, March 2023, 3:06:02); Knickerbocker Canyon Trail Run (Half marathon, March 2023, 2:35:53); Folsom Lake Falcon Crest Trail Run (Half marathon, April 2023, 2:25:27); Woodside/Purisima Creek Crossover (Half marathon, April 2023, 2:40:52); Folsom Lake Trail Run (35K, May 2023, 3:51:54); Bryce Canyon Ultras (50K, May 2023, 8:41:08); Marin Ultra Challenge (50K, June 2023, 6:41:54); SF Marathon (Marathon, July 2023, 4:12:29); Berkeley Half Marathon (Half marathon, November 2023, 1:44:37); Mt. Umunhum Trail Conquest – Winter (Half marathon, February 2024, 2:33:29); Chabot 30K (30K, February 2024, 3:24:21); CAF Half Marathon (Half marathon, February 2026, 2:28:18); Valencia Half Marathon (Half marathon, May 2026, 2:40:26).
